title: 12 Aug 2026 (Jeddah)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Jeddah, 12 August 2026

questions.question: A child suddenly cannot stand after an URTI. Examination is normal except for ataxia, and CT brain is normal. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Post-viral (varicella, influenza) cerebellitis gives acute ataxia with normal imaging and recovers over weeks.

questions.question: A 4-month-old weighed 3.5 kg at birth. Head circumference was 35 cm at birth and is now 47 cm, length 50 to 60 cm, and the mother reports no change in suckling. What do you do?
questions.exp: HC has crossed centiles fast (47 cm is well above the 98th centile at 4 months), so image the brain. With an open fontanelle and a well baby, cranial ultrasound is first; most recalls key US when suckling is unchanged and MRI when the baby is unwell.

questions.question: A toddler has breath-holding attacks. What is the management?
questions.exp: Breath-holding spells are benign; check iron status and reassure.

questions.question: Which feature carries a worse prognosis in neuroblastoma?
questions.exp: N-MYC amplification, age over 18 months and unfavourable histology are poor prognostic factors. Age under 1 year is favourable; the recall writer marked "age under 1" then corrected to N-MYC.

questions.question: A child has Guillain-Barré syndrome with progressive weakness. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: IVIG or plasma exchange. Steroids do not help.

questions.question: An infant in shock has a left tension pneumothorax. What is the immediate treatment?
questions.exp: Tension pneumothorax with shock needs immediate needle thoracocentesis, then a chest drain.

questions.question: A boy has eye blinking, then throat clearing, and years later another tic. How is it diagnosed?
questions.exp: Tourette syndrome is clinical.

questions.question: A 10-year-old girl fell from a horse. GCS is 10, pupils react, cough and gag reflexes are present, she is bradypnoeic, and spinal X-rays are normal. What do you do?
questions.exp: Spinal cord injury without radiological abnormality (SCIWORA) is common in children; MRI shows the cord injury.

questions.question: A child has signs of meningitis. Rapid H. influenzae test is negative and ceftriaxone has been started. What is your action?
questions.exp: A negative rapid antigen test does not exclude bacterial meningitis; continue and add vancomycin if not improving.
questions.a: Continue treatment until culture results are available

questions.question: A 4-year-old after a road accident has GCS 5, heart rate 52 and respiratory rate 8. What do you do?
questions.exp: Airway and breathing first: intubate and ventilate; bradycardia below 60 with poor perfusion despite ventilation needs CPR.
questions.a: Intubate and ventilate (start CPR if HR stays below 60 with poor perfusion)

questions.question: After head trauma a child is well in the ER, then after a while becomes drowsy. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: A lucid interval followed by deterioration is classic extradural haematoma.

questions.question: A 2-month-old fell from the bed, has a decreased conscious level (GCS 10), bruises on the back and a bulging fontanelle. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: A short fall rarely causes this. Subdural haemorrhage with bruises in a young infant suggests abusive head trauma.

questions.question: An infant fell head down from the stairs, was fully conscious immediately after, then a few hours later had an impaired conscious level. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lucid interval = extradural haematoma.

questions.question: A child with seizures was given 2 doses of lorazepam in the ambulance and is still fitting. What do you give now?
questions.exp: After two benzodiazepine doses, give a second-line drug (phenytoin, levetiracetam or valproate).

questions.question: A child has proximal weakness and a typical rash of juvenile dermatomyositis. What is the first test?
questions.exp: CK is raised in most cases.

questions.question: A child has convulsions and hypopigmented skin patches. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Ash-leaf macules, shagreen patch, angiofibromas, retinal hamartomas and cardiac rhabdomyomas are TS features.

questions.question: A CT picture shows a brain abscess. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Cover streptococci, anaerobes and staphylococci; drain if large.

questions.question: A 10-month-old with otitis media on amoxicillin for 5 days becomes irritable. What do you do?
questions.exp: Suspect meningitis and do an LP.

questions.question: A child has recurrent abdominal pain with headache. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Episodic abdominal pain with headache and family history suggests migraine.

questions.question: A child has lower limb hypotonia, reduced reflexes and a positive Babinski sign. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Acute cord lesions cause flaccid weakness with an upgoing plantar (spinal shock), with a sensory level and bladder involvement.

questions.question: A child with nephrotic syndrome on steroids has severe bilateral flank pain, WBC 22 with neutrophilia, urine WBC 2 and RBC 1500. What is the best investigation?
questions.exp: Nephrotic syndrome is hypercoagulable; flank pain with haematuria suggests renal vein thrombosis, seen on Doppler.
questions.d: Doppler ultrasound of the renal veins

questions.question: A 12-year-old girl has dark urine, abdominal pain, high BP, fever 39, urine protein ++, RBC >10 and WBC >10. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Haematuria with hypertension (nephritic picture) suggests acute GN.

questions.question: A 6-year-old girl, previously well, develops nocturnal enuresis and lower abdominal pain. Urine has WBC >10, RBC >10 and protein 2+. BP 110/73 and CBC is normal except anaemia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: New enuresis with abdominal pain and pyuria suggests UTI. BP is not high enough for GN.

questions.question: A 3-year-old uncircumcised boy has dark urine, fever and abdominal pain. How do you collect urine?
questions.exp: In an ill or untrained child, SPA or catheter gives the most reliable sample.

questions.question: A 1-year-old with constipation has oliguria and haematuria. What is the best investigation to differentiate the cause?
questions.exp: UTI is the most common cause of haematuria in children; constipation predisposes to it.

questions.question: A child has iron deficiency anaemia on treatment. Which parameter rises first?
questions.exp: Reticulocytes rise in 3-5 days; Hb rises after 1-2 weeks.

questions.question: A child has bruises, giant platelets and thrombocytopenia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bernard-Soulier (GPIb deficiency) gives giant platelets, low count and absent ristocetin aggregation.

questions.question: A child with sickle cell disease has recurrent pneumonia. What immune defect explains it?
questions.exp: Autosplenectomy and impaired alternative complement (properdin) pathway predispose to encapsulated bacteria.
questions.b: Functional asplenia with impaired humoral immunity and low properdin activity

questions.question: Which of these is a vitamin K-dependent factor?
questions.exp: Vitamin K-dependent: factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S.

questions.question: A child has dark skin pigmentation and pancytopenia. What do you do?
questions.exp: Fanconi anaemia: confirm marrow failure; HSCT is curative.
questions.d: Bone marrow aspiration (and transplant if treatment is needed)

questions.question: A boy has scrotal redness and acute abdominal pain (epididymo-orchitis). What is the likely organism?
questions.exp: In prepubertal boys, epididymitis is often linked to urinary tract anomalies and coliforms.

questions.question: A child with TOF has a hypercyanotic spell with tachycardia and tachypnoea. Central pulse is good. What drug prevents further spells?
questions.exp: Acute spell: oxygen, knee-chest, morphine, fluids, IV propranolol or phenylephrine. Oral propranolol prevents spells until surgery.

questions.question: What is an indication for hospital admission in a child with croup?
questions.exp: Cyanosis or stridor at rest with distress need admission.

questions.question: A child after a car accident has low GCS, HR 60 and respiratory rate 8. What do you do?
questions.exp: Secure the airway and ventilate; start CPR if HR stays below 60 with poor perfusion.

questions.question: A 9-month-old weighing 5 kg has a VSD with cardiomegaly, RV and LV heaves, a palpable P2 and saturation 93%, on diuretic, digoxin and captopril. What is next?
questions.exp: Failure to thrive with pulmonary hypertension despite medical therapy needs urgent repair.

questions.question: After an arterial switch operation a child develops an arrhythmia on ECG. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Recalls key sick sinus syndrome for post-TGA surgery arrhythmia.

questions.question: An ECG shows wide QRS and peaked T waves in a child with leg numbness. What do you give first?
questions.exp: Calcium stabilises the myocardium first; then shift potassium.

questions.question: A child is irritable with respiratory distress and HR 210; the ECG shows SVT. What do you give?
questions.exp: Adenosine IV rapid bolus.

questions.question: A child has an ejection systolic murmur and a widely fixed split S2. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Fixed splitting = ASD.

questions.question: After an accident resuscitation is started, and the ECG shows organised electrical activity without a pulse. What is the rhythm?
questions.exp: PEA is treated with CPR and adrenaline, looking for reversible causes.

questions.question: Which lesion most often leads to pulmonary hypertension?
questions.exp: Large left-to-right shunts at ventricular level (VSD) cause early pulmonary vascular disease.

questions.question: A 3-month-old has hepatomegaly, tachypnoea, tachycardia and a pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Heart failure with a pansystolic murmur at the LLSB is a large VSD.

questions.question: A baby is cyanosed 12 hours after birth. The chest X-ray shows clear (oligaemic) lungs without a structural lesion. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Cyanosis with clear lungs and no heart lesion on echo suggests PPHN.
questions.a: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn

questions.question: A 7-year-old has fever for 15 days, bone pain, mild hepatosplenomegaly and a grade 4 apical murmur. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Prolonged fever, splenomegaly and a significant murmur suggest endocarditis; take serial blood cultures.

questions.question: After 2 hours, what amount of a meal remaining in the stomach is abnormal (delayed gastric emptying)?
questions.exp: On scintigraphy, retention above about 60% at 2 hours or 10% at 4 hours is delayed; the recall keyed 40-50%.

questions.question: A 2-week-old has bilious vomiting, constipation and abdominal pain. How is it diagnosed?
questions.exp: Upper GI contrast shows the abnormal duodenojejunal flexure and volvulus.

questions.question: A 7-year-old has stool incontinence, normal growth and an anal fissure. What do you do?
questions.exp: Soiling usually means overflow from constipation.

questions.question: A 1-year-old had repair of Hirschsprung disease at 2 days and now has fever, abdominal pain and distension. What do you do?
questions.exp: Hirschsprung enterocolitis: washouts, IV fluids and antibiotics.

questions.question: A child with diarrhoea and vomiting has slightly delayed skin turgor and a moist mouth. What do you give?
questions.exp: Mild dehydration is treated with ORS.

questions.question: How does isolated tracheo-oesophageal fistula with oesophageal atresia appear on X-ray?
questions.exp: The NG tube coils in the blind upper pouch.
questions.a: NG tube coiled in the upper oesophagus

questions.question: A baby has vomiting, abdominal pain and severe distension; X-ray shows multiple fluid levels. What do you do?
questions.exp: Intestinal obstruction needs surgical assessment.

questions.question: An adolescent has chronic recurrent abdominal pain, altered bowel habit, weight loss and anaemia. What is the next investigation?
questions.exp: Suspected IBD needs endoscopy with biopsy.

questions.question: A child had contact with hepatitis A and now has jaundice and high liver enzymes. What is the test?
questions.exp: Anti-HAV IgM confirms acute hepatitis A.

questions.question: A 2-week-old neonate began vomiting on day 10; today the vomit is green, with distension, tenderness and bloody mucous stool. What do you do first?
questions.exp: Bloody stools with distension suggest NEC or volvulus: stop feeds, decompress, give antibiotics and image.
questions.d: Stop oral feeds (nil by mouth, NG decompression)

questions.question: What is part of the secondary survey in trauma?
questions.exp: The secondary survey is the head-to-toe examination after ABCDE.

questions.question: A child has acute abdominal pain, tenderness, scrotal oedema and nephrotic-range lab results. What is the most likely organism of the peritonitis?
questions.exp: Primary peritonitis in nephrotic syndrome is most often pneumococcal. The recall writer chose E. coli.

questions.question: A picture shows bowel protruding through a defect beside the umbilicus without a covering sac. What is it?
questions.exp: Gastroschisis has no sac and lies right of the cord.

questions.question: A girl has disorganised speech, visual and auditory hallucinations and a father with a similar illness. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Hallucinations and disorganised speech with family history suggest early-onset schizophrenia.

questions.question: A girl developed normally until 2 years, then stopped responding to questions, looks at the sky and has repetitive movements. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Regression of social communication with stereotypies is the recall's keyed autism; Rett has hand-wringing and acquired microcephaly.

questions.question: How is thumb sucking managed?
questions.exp: Praise and rewards for not sucking work best.

questions.question: A 12-year-old has jaundice and liver fibrosis with an echogenic pattern on ultrasound. Autoimmune liver disease is suspected. Which antibodies do you test first?
questions.exp: Autoimmune hepatitis (ANA/ASMA type 1, anti-LKM type 2) and sclerosing cholangitis are the autoimmune liver diseases of childhood. The recall keyed antimitochondrial antibody, which marks primary biliary cholangitis, an adult disease.
questions.c: ANA, anti-smooth muscle and anti-LKM antibodies

questions.question: Which is a vitamin K-dependent coagulation protein?
questions.exp: II, VII, IX, X, protein C and S.

questions.question: A girl's target height is calculated from her parents' heights. Which formula is used?
questions.exp: Girls subtract 13 cm from the father's height before averaging.

questions.question: A child has recurrent episodes of vomiting with well periods in between. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Stereotyped episodes of vomiting with normal health between are cyclic vomiting, a migraine variant.

questions.question: A child has a 10 kg weight and 5% dehydration. What is the total fluid for 24 hours?
questions.exp: Maintenance 100 × 10 = 1000 mL plus deficit 5% × 10 kg = 500 mL, total 1500 mL.

questions.question: What is the most common mechanism of testicular torsion in adolescents?
questions.exp: Intravaginal torsion (bell-clapper deformity) is typical after the neonatal period.

questions.question: A child with a febrile seizure (temp 40) for 1 minute is now stable with fever 39 in the ER. What do you do?
questions.exp: Simple febrile seizures need reassurance; antipyretics do not prevent recurrence.
questions.a: Reassure and treat the fever for comfort

questions.question: A child with an allergy develops anaphylaxis with swollen lips. After IM adrenaline, what do you give next?
questions.exp: After adrenaline, give fluids if needed; steroids and antihistamines are adjuncts.

questions.question: A child needs special care during examination because it may provoke airway obstruction. Which condition?
questions.exp: Do not examine the throat or upset the child.

questions.question: A 10 kg child is in cardiac arrest. Which is correct?
questions.exp: Compress 100-120/min; adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg = 0.1 mL/kg of 1:10,000 (1 mL for 10 kg).

questions.question: A child has signs of hyperthyroidism. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Antithyroid drugs are first line in children.

questions.question: A child has pneumonia with Gram-positive diplococci. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Pneumococcal pneumonia: IV ceftriaxone (or penicillin) without combination.

questions.question: A child with suspected immunodeficiency is awaiting results. Which vaccines should be held?
questions.exp: Live vaccines are held until immunity is known.

questions.question: An HIV-positive child needs vaccines. Which can be given?
questions.exp: Inactivated vaccines are safe; live vaccines depend on CD4 count.

questions.question: A child has severe dehydration. Which sign is expected?
questions.exp: Severe dehydration: prolonged CRT, sunken eyes, lethargy, tachycardia.

questions.question: Where is it best to build a new children's hospital?
questions.exp: Services should be placed where the need is (distributive justice).
questions.c: In an area with many children

questions.question: A mother refuses to attend the breaking of bad news. What do you do?
questions.exp: Respect the mother's wish and continue with the other parent.

questions.question: A mother wants to stop ventilation for her baby but feels guilty. What is needed?
questions.exp: Withdrawal decisions need consensus of senior doctors (often two consultants) with the family.

questions.question: A do-not-resuscitate order requires agreement of how many doctors?
questions.exp: In Saudi regulations a DNR needs three physicians including the treating consultant.

questions.question: What is the definition of procedural justice?
questions.exp: Procedural justice concerns fair processes.
questions.a: Fair and consistent processes and rules applied to everyone

questions.question: A doctor works in an MOH hospital and in private practice. What should he follow?
questions.exp: Dual practice must follow MOH regulations to avoid conflict of interest.

questions.question: How should a patient be identified before a procedure?
questions.exp: Use two identifiers (full three-part name and MRN), never bed number.
questions.a: With two identifiers, such as full name and medical record number

questions.question: A child injured while riding a bike has lockjaw and generalised muscle spasms. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Trismus with spasms after a wound is tetanus.

questions.question: A child with diarrhoea needs admission and C. difficile is suspected. What precautions are needed?
questions.exp: Spores resist alcohol; use gloves, gown and soap and water.
questions.d: Contact precautions with soap-and-water hand washing

questions.question: A child with a BAHA implant had purulent ear discharge. A junior gave antibiotics without culture or senior advice, and later the implant needed reassessment. What should be followed to prevent this?
questions.exp: Safety failures are addressed by fixing systems, handover and escalation policies.
questions.b: Systematic processes and policies (clear handover and escalation)

questions.question: A doctor connects oxygen tubing to an IV cannula, harming the patient. What type of error is this?
questions.exp: An unsafe act by the person at the sharp end is an active failure (Reason's model).

questions.question: What makes research on a new drug ethical?
questions.exp: Voluntary informed consent with full disclosure is essential.

questions.question: A mother cannot recall her child's vaccine history. The child is 4-6 years old. What do you do?
questions.exp: Undocumented vaccines are treated as not given; give the due vaccines.
questions.a: Restart the whole schedule from birth

questions.question: A neutropenic child on chemotherapy has fever with no focus. Which organism must empirical antibiotics always cover?
questions.exp: Febrile neutropenia is treated at once with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime), because Gram-negative sepsis can kill within hours.

questions.question: A 7-year-old girl has fever for 15 days, poor activity, bone pain, mild hepatosplenomegaly and a murmur. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Prolonged fever with splenomegaly and a murmur: think endocarditis.

questions.question: A 7-year-old girl has facial and sacral swelling, fatigue, a grade 4 apical murmur, mildly low albumin and mildly high triglycerides. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: The writer chose heart failure because albumin was only mildly low and there was a significant murmur. Nephrotic syndrome needs albumin below 25 g/L with heavy proteinuria.

questions.question: An asthmatic child was caught in a house fire. What is the most important investigation?
questions.exp: Pulse oximetry is falsely normal in CO poisoning; measure COHb.

questions.question: A family was in a fire; all have carboxyhaemoglobin below 25%. What do you give?
questions.exp: High-flow 100% oxygen; hyperbaric oxygen for severe cases.

questions.question: A child has meningococcaemia. What is the organism?
questions.exp: Purpuric rash with shock is meningococcal sepsis.

questions.question: A neonate has cyanosis during feeding that improves with crying, an ear anomaly and a heart murmur. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: CHARGE: coloboma, heart defects, choanal atresia, growth retardation, genital and ear anomalies.

questions.question: A 2-3-week-old with an NG tube draining green aspirate was seen by a junior who ordered investigations the senior thought unnecessary. What should be done?
questions.exp: Bilious aspirate needs an urgent upper GI contrast study for malrotation. The recall writer was unsure.

questions.question: Parents are both carriers of sickle cell trait. What is the chance of an affected child in each pregnancy?
questions.exp: Autosomal recessive: 1 in 4.

questions.question: A picture shows a pale child's hand next to his father's; the child has severe anaemia with heart failure. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Anaemic heart failure needs slow packed-cell transfusion.

questions.question: A picture shows blisters on the hands and feet of an infant with epidermolysis bullosa. What is the priority?
questions.exp: Wound care and infection prevention are the mainstay.
questions.a: Prevent infection and protect the skin

questions.question: Which skin disease shows a positive Koebner phenomenon?
questions.exp: Lesions appear at sites of trauma in psoriasis, lichen planus and vitiligo.

questions.question: A newborn with Rh incompatibility had UVC and UAC lines and then developed haematuria. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Catheters and polycythaemia predispose to RVT.

questions.question: A child has had headache for a long time and now vomiting and ataxia. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Posterior fossa tumour (medulloblastoma) gives morning headache, vomiting and ataxia.

questions.question: A child with ALL has a long-line infection. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Broad cover including MRSA.

questions.question: A picture shows a hypotonic infant with a protruding tongue and macrocephaly. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Macroglossia, hypotonia and umbilical hernia suggest congenital hypothyroidism.

questions.question: A child has acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: MRI shows multifocal demyelination.

questions.question: A returning traveller has fever, reduced consciousness and a blood film with parasites. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Falciparum malaria with coma is cerebral malaria.
